newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia to start new trading in Gazprom shares.
newsitem.headline: Russia to start new trading in Gazprom shares.

text.p: Russia plans to launch electronic trading in natural gas monopoly Gazprom on December 11, an official from the body organising the trading said on Thursday.
Currently Gazprom shares are traded in Russia in the Russian Trading System (RTS), a local version of NASDAQ, but traders there require Gazprom's permission to sell shares.
The new system gives traders participating in the trading the right to buy shares without asking Gazprom for permission.
The Federal Securities Corporation (FFK) which organises the trading expects about 20 dealers to take part, FFK administrative director Alexandra Levitskaya told Reuters.
The FFK plans to hold three trading sessions this year -- on December 11, 18 and 26 -- and in the second half of January switch to daily trading, Levitskaya said.
The new system will only trade shares which had been sold at weekly cash auctions organised by the FFK, she said.
"The trade system turnover will increase as the inflow from the weekly auctions rises," Levitskaya said.
Gazprom closed at $0.332 after $0.335 at Wednesday's close in RTS.
A lot volume will be 10,000 shares and the volume of trade and the price will depend on the brokers' interest, Levitskaya said.
At the last cash auction on December 4 an average price of Gazprom share fell to 1,807.14 roubles (32 cents) from 1,873.40 roubles at the previous auction.
The corporation will offer 250,000 Gazprom shares at the next auction on December 18.

Gazprom is one of Russia's biggest companies by market capitalisation, but its shares are among Russia's most illiquid, because company rules state that shares must be offered to Gazprom before being sold.
If Gazprom does not take up the option to buy the shares within 30 days, the owner can sell them within another 90 days.
Gazprom organised the weekly auctions through the FFK starting in March to create an orderly market in its paper.
